Enrico Caruso (tenor), Victor Orchestra (orchestra) Documented

DAHR names the Victor Orchestra, but no conductor or session instrumentation is established. The usual opera full score is not evidence of acoustic-session substitutions.

Work version
Unknown Unknown

Acoustic recording of the named excerpt. Performing edition, cuts and studio instrumental substitutions are unestablished. No instrument-by-instrument timeline is supplied; the modern opera full score does not document this session.

[1]
Recorded
1909-11-06 Documented

DAHR and the current Commons description agree on 6 November 1909. The candidate’s 11 June is not retained; this is not a US/European ambiguous-date conversion.

City/place as stated in the cited recording source; no more precise room or studio inferred.

Adam Cuerden — restoration; original digitisation engineer unestablished Documented

Commons documents click and hiss removal and links an unrestored counterpart. The uploader is not credited as the original digitisation engineer.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date established. The Commons, Archive and YouTube upload dates are not treated as digitisation or restoration dates.

[1]
Processing
Click and hiss removal; restored Ogg Vorbis supplied to Commons Documented

Only the described processing is documented; no equipment, filter settings, pitch correction or speed correction is inferred.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying Puccini composition and historical libretto are public domain where ordinary life-plus-70 terms apply; no modern edition is claimed cleared. Documented

Commons marks the historical work public domain. This does not by itself establish the sound recording’s rights; the recording basis is separately documented below.

[1] [9]
Recording rights
Rule 2 — United States public domain: original sound recording commercially issued in 1909, before 1923. Documented

DAHR’s Victor 87043 issue MARC gives [1909]; Moses places the issue in the 1909–⁠1911 release group. Commons’ PD-US label is therefore supported by sound-recording issue evidence, not merely Puccini’s death year. No claim of worldwide clearance.

[1] [3] [8] [10]

Giacomo Puccini, Tosca: Recondita armonia. Enrico Caruso and Victor Orchestra, Camden, 6 November 1909, B-8347-1. Internet Archive Caruso_part2 via Wikimedia Commons; restoration by Adam Cuerden. Rights statement

  1. Wikimedia Commons — Caruso, Recondita armonia — Description identifies matrix B-8347 and 6 November 1909; Source, PD-US/PD-old tags, click/hiss removal and unrestored counterpart; MP3 derivative. Inspected description separately from embedded metadata.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. DAHR — Victor matrix B-8347 — Tenor and Victor Orchestra; take 1, 6 November 1909, Camden; Victor and Gramophone issues. Later electrically re-orchestrated dubs are listed separately and are not asserted for this source.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. DAHR — Victor 87043 — MARC 264: Victor [1909]; B-8347, take 1, 10-inch single-faced Red Seal; work, singer and orchestral description.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Internet Archive — Collected Works of Caruso part 2 metadata — Source 78; no licenseurl in the opened metadata. Publicdate/addeddate in 2004 are repository dates, not the recording session.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Internet Archive — Caruso part 2 file list — Caruso-⁠Reconditaarmonia.mp3, original 128 kbps MP3, about 2:25; Ogg derivative. A separate ReconditeArmonia file also exists: it is not silently substituted. Commons identifies the restored file’s source item, not a uniquely proven carrier.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Recondita armonia — aria text — Italian text: contrasting hair and eyes; art combines beauties; final thought remains Tosca. Consulted for passage-general textual explanation, not word-level timing.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Opéra national de Paris — Tosca, 2025–⁠26 — Acts I–III synopses; Roman locations, painter and Attavanti, Scarpia’s coercion, letter before execution. Used for dramatic context, not timings.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. Julian Morton Moses — American Celebrity Recordings 1900–⁠1925, UCSB Historical Discographies edition — Introduction explains that artist sections group records by release years, not session dates. Caruso: Victor Red Seal 1906–⁠1908 includes 89006 and 95200; 1909–⁠1911 includes 87043. Destinn: Victor Red Seal 1914–⁠1917 includes 88487. Opened as extracted text; not used to infer exact take or transfer pressing.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Puccini Festival — Giacomo Puccini — Biography and work entries: early church work, Milan studies, librettists, source authors, premieres, composer’s death in 1924.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  10. U.S. Copyright Office — Classics Protection and Access Act — Term: recordings first published before 1923 ceased receiving the specified federal remedies after 31 December 2021. Sound-recording basis, distinct from composition copyright.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
